packet.headline_seed: German tourist wins payout after losing sun lounger race
packet.description_seed: The man sued his tour operator for allowing people to reserve sun loungers with towels despite a hotel ban on the practice.

what: German tourist wins payout after losing sun lounger race

clean_source_blocks.text: The man sued his tour operator for allowing people to reserve sun loungers with towels despite a hotel ban on the practice.
A German tourist has won a payout of more than €900 (£850) after he was unable to secure a sun lounger due to other guests reserving them with towels.
A furious German tourist went to court and won a payout after he failed to get a sun lounger on holiday, despite waking up at 6am.

The dad-of-two said he dropped around £6,200 (€7,186) on a package holiday to the Greek island of Kos with his two children and wife, back in August 2024. The man, who was not named, said he spent around 20 minutes each day trying to find sun loungers where all four family members could sit together. He said most sunbeds had already been taken by guests who put their towels down, despite the hotel having a rule explicitly against this.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
A German tourist has won a payout of more than €900 (£850) after he was unable to secure a sun lounger due to other guests reserving them with towels.

The man, who has not been identified, was on holiday in Greece with his family in 2024, and said he spent 20 minutes a day trying to find a sun lounger, despite waking up at 06:00.

He then sued his tour operator for allowing the reservation system, arguing the sunbeds were reserved so often, they were unusable.

Judges at a district court in Hanover ruled in his favour, and said the family of four were entitled to a larger refund on their package holiday as it had been "defective".

The man had initially paid €7,186 (£6211) to take his wife and their two children on the package holiday to Kos, an island in Greece.

In his arguments to court, he said that his tour operator had failed to enforce the resort's ban on towel reserving, and did not confront guests who were engaging in the practice.

He added that even when his family rose at 06:00, loungers were unavailable, and his children were forced to lie on the floor.

Though the tour operator had initially paid out a refund of €350 (£302), judges in Hanover ruled the family was entitled to a refund of €986.70 (£852.89).

They said that although the travel company did not run the hotel and could not ensure every customer could access a sunbed at any given time, the operator did have an obligation to make sure there was an organisational structure that would guarantee a "reasonable" ratio of sunbeds to guests.

Many tourists will have encountered "sunbed wars" or "dawn dash" on holiday, which is the practice of reserving loungers with towels.

Last year, videos circulating on social media suggested holiday-goers in Tenerife were sleeping on sun loungers in order to secure a poolside spot.

Some tour companies are trying to combat the practice, with operator Thomas Cook offering tourists the option to pre-book a spot beside the pool for an additional fee.

In Spain, tourists in certain regions have been threatened with a €250 fine for reserving a sun lounger and then disappearing for hours.

[Lähde: The Mirror]
A furious German tourist went to court and won a payout after he failed to get a sun lounger on holiday, despite waking up at 6am.

The dad-of-two said he dropped around £6,200 (€7,186) on a package holiday to the Greek island of Kos with his two children and wife, back in August 2024. The man, who was not named, said he spent around 20 minutes each day trying to find sun loungers where all four family members could sit together. He said most sunbeds had already been taken by guests who put their towels down, despite the hotel having a rule explicitly against this.

The dad, who sued a tour operator at a district court in Hanover, said even at 6am most of the sunbeds had been "taken" meaning his two kids were often forced to lie on the floor.

He also claimed workers at the hotel failed to intervene and enforce their own policy against reserving spots with a towels in advance.

The furious man took the case to a German court and the judge sided with him, as the court found the package holiday was "defective" as the family did not get the "character" they would have expected as a contractual right.

While the tour operator did not run the large Greek hotel the family had been staying at, the judge said it had an obligation to make sure each customer could have access to a sunbed during their stay.

The judge also said the travel company needed to make sure the hotel could ensure there was a "reasonable" ratio of sun loungers to tourists.

payload.title: Saksalaisturisti sai korvauksia aurinkotuolikiistasta
payload.summary: Saksalainen pakettimatkailija vei matkanjärjestäjän oikeuteen, kun hotellin aurinkotuoleja varattiin pyyhkeillä kiellosta huolimatta. Hänelle määrättiin yli 900 euron korvaus.
payload.content:
Saksalainen turisti on saanut yli 900 euron korvauksen kiistassa, joka koski lomahotellin aurinkotuolien varaamista pyyhkeillä. Mies katsoi, että matkanjärjestäjä oli sallinut käytännön jatkumisen, vaikka hotellilla oli sääntö, jonka mukaan aurinkotuoleja ei saanut varata etukäteen pyyhkeillä.

## Kiista alkoi lomalla Kosilla

Nimettömänä pysynyt mies oli perheensä kanssa pakettimatkalla Kreikan Kosin saarella elokuussa 2024. Matkalla olivat mukana hänen vaimonsa ja kaksi lastaan. Pakettimatkan hinnaksi on kerrottu noin 7 186 euroa.

Miehen mukaan perheen oli vaikea löytää aurinkotuoleja, joilla kaikki neljä perheenjäsentä olisivat voineet olla yhdessä. Hän kertoi käyttäneensä päivittäin noin 20 minuuttia sopivien paikkojen etsimiseen. Ongelman taustalla oli hänen mukaansa se, että muut hotellivieraat olivat varanneet suuren osan aurinkotuoleista jättämällä niille pyyhkeitä.

Käytäntö oli miehen mukaan erityisen turhauttava siksi, että hotellissa oli nimenomainen sääntö tällaista varaamista vastaan. Hän kertoi myös heränneensä jo aamukuudelta yrittääkseen saada aurinkotuolit perheelleen, mutta siitä huolimatta paikkojen löytäminen epäonnistui.

## Oikeus määräsi korvauksen

Mies haastoi matkanjärjestäjän oikeuteen. Hänen väitteensä oli, että matkanjärjestäjä ei ollut puuttunut riittävästi siihen, että hotellivieraat rikkoivat aurinkotuolien varaamista koskevaa kieltoa.

Oikeusratkaisun seurauksena mies sai yli 900 euron korvauksen. Korvaus ei siis perustunut pelkästään siihen, että aurinkotuolia ei löytynyt, vaan siihen, että hotellin omaa sääntöä ei miehen mukaan valvottu käytännössä riittävästi osana lomapalvelua.

## Tapaus nostaa esiin hotellien käytännöt

Tapaus on poikkeuksellinen esimerkki siitä, miten lomahotellien arkipäiväisiltä vaikuttavat käytännöt voivat johtaa oikeudelliseen riitaan. Aurinkotuolien varaaminen pyyhkeillä on monissa lomakohteissa tuttu ilmiö, mutta tässä tapauksessa ratkaisevaa oli se, että hotellilla kerrottiin olleen selkeä kielto, jonka noudattaminen jäi matkailijan mukaan puutteelliseksi.

Aineistossa ei kerrota miehen nimeä eikä tarkempaa tuomioistuinta. Tiedossa on kuitenkin, että kyse oli pakettimatkasta, perheen lomasta Kosilla ja kiistasta, jossa hotellin oma sääntö sekä sen käytännön valvonta nousivat korvausratkaisun keskiöön.
